title: Destruction of Evidence
text: I saw a cold sweat trickling down Father’s forehead. Keel, Yuki-chan, and the others—along with the Assistant and Rival—stepped down from the carriage and assumed battle stances. It looks like they’re ready to engage in combat at a moment’s notice, depending on how things play out. Well, it’s as if they’ve already launched a preemptive strike.
“You… no, do any of you even understand what you’ve done?!”
“Shields are evil! It was decided from the very beginning! You and that traitorous, sell-out princess will both be wiped out!”
Undeterred, he’s raising his sword toward Father again. It seems Magic is imbued in the sword… but it can’t even scratch Father right now.
“What are you doing to my brother?!”
“I won’t let you!”
Keel quickly closes in and slashes at the knight’s sword-wielding hand, while Sakura-chan delivers a kick and simultaneously slices him to pieces with her sword.
“Guhahaaaaaa!”
From behind, the knights cast Magic, raining down a storm of fire—on their own allies as well.
“Shooting Star Shield… wait, that’s impossible!”
Since my Finacée isn’t part of our group, my Father realizes that casting a Shooting Star Shield would just deflect the attack, so he spreads his robe wide to deflect the rain of fire.
“Second Shield!”
Then he summons a second shield and shields my Finacée. Thanks to his robe, none of us have suffered any injuries.
“Not yet. Focus your magic even more!”
“…Drifa Absorb.”
I’ll raise my spear and absorb their magic. Against a bunch like this, I can even nullify Ceremonial Magic.
“Guh…”

The knights who brought my Finacée are trying to escape on horseback. To turn their backs in the heat of battle is utterly ridiculous. Above all, to abandon the princess they’re supposed to protect and run—what a despicable bunch they are.
“I won’t let them get away!”

I end the Absorb spell and start running after them. Because of the distance, Filolial-sama, Keel, my Assistant, and my Rival are a step behind. Well, they’ll probably catch up, but trying to hurt my Father and my Finacée deserves a thousand deaths.
“Aiming Lancer X!”
After locking on, I hurled my lance high into the sky. The lance split into countless fragments, piercing every single knight who tried to flee. I brought them all down—horses and all—with a thud.
“Guh—”
“Th-this… this is ridiculous. According to our reports, they were supposed to be much weaker… Why… are they so—”

Every single one of them died in a single blow. There’s no need to leave any survivors, after all. Hahahah! This is my Father’s strategy. Since the enemy thinks we’re weak, it makes them easier to take down—which is just fine by me.
“Now then, let’s recover the video crystals.”

I picked up the video crystals the knights had dropped and channeled my Magical Power into them. My father and my fiancée appear on the screen. It’s slightly different from what I remember. The footage I saw before had been altered, but in it, my father had his arm around my fiancée’s neck with a sinister look on his face.

I can’t help but recall the sight of that Trash and that Crimson Swine tearfully begging me to rescue my fiancée from my father. How disingenuous. It seems the Trash was being sincere, but I know the Crimson Swine was actually trying to get my Finacée killed.
Anyway, it seems a bit premature, but it’s now clear they’ve played the “Finacée” card to put my Father on the wanted list.
“Now they can’t fabricate any more evidence videos claiming my Father committed the kidnapping.”
“Isn’t this going a bit too far…?”

My father said this as he looked down at the body lying on the ground. As always, he’s such a kind man. But if we let him escape, our situation will only get worse. Don’t worry. I’ll handle all the dirty work myself. After all…
“A knight turned his blade on his own country’s princess and then fled, didn’t he? Keeping him alive won’t lead to anything good.”
“I suppose so, but…”
“Ah… uu…”
My Finacée looks back and forth between me and my Father with a stunned expression.
“Are you okay?”
“Huh!?”
Seeing my Finacée flinch in fear, Father scratches his cheek with a troubled look.

“We can’t have a proper conversation until you calm down… You probably can’t relax with a corpse lying around here, so let’s move somewhere else. “Someone, please bring over the carriage Melty rode in.”
“I’ll do it!”
With that, Kou goes and brings over the carriage my Finacée rode in. My Finacée is so shaken she’s practically frozen in place, trembling.
“Are you okay?”

Sakura-chan is gently patting my Finacée to calm her down. She’s using her body to block the view of the corpse. Seeing a glimpse of Sakura-chan’s kindness warms my heart. The finacée, who’s on the verge of hyperventilating, seems to have calmed down a bit thanks to Sakura-chan’s soothing words.
“Um… first off, Melty—is that okay to call you? Try to stay calm and listen.”
“Y-yes.”
“It seems the knights who brought you here were plotting some kind of conspiracy and were planning to kill you right in front of us… is that right?”
The finacée looked in the direction of the corpse lying on the ground and nodded quietly.

“Of course, I’m not just saying this without any basis. They were making a big fuss about how ‘the Shield is definitely evil’ and how they’d ‘deliberately taken the princess hostage.’ If you want, I’ll even escort you back. We have no intention of kidnapping you or wreaking havoc on your country.”

My finacée, who had been calmed down by Sakura-chan, nodded with a determined look in her eyes. True to his status as her Finacée, though he hadn’t quite grasped the situation at first, he’d regained his composure.
“It seems I’ve brought disaster upon the Holy Ones of the Divine Bird… no, wait. It seems I’ve brought disaster upon the Shield and Spear Heroes and their party. I’m so sorry.”
“Don’t worry about it. You’re a victim too.”
“…Thank you. I’m glad to see that the Shield Hero is indeed a man of integrity, just as my mother said.”
“By ‘my mother’… you mean the Queen of Melromarc, right? She’s higher in rank than the King who summoned us.”
“Yes. My mother ordered me to mediate between my father and the Heroes. However, I’m truly sorry that things have turned out this way.”

Something about my Finacée’s way of speaking just doesn’t sit right with me. Did she always speak so politely? I seem to recall her speaking more hysterically, like, “There’s no way I’m giving Filo-chan to someone like you!” She spoke to my Father in a similarly commanding tone—she hardly ever used polite language with him.

“That’s fine. But to be honest, I don’t think I’ll be able to get along with your father. We have no intention of getting involved in the war; we just want to focus on challenging the waves, which is the true duty of a hero. As long as he doesn’t understand that…”
“…I see. I also think my father and older sister are at fault in this matter. Once we’ve returned safely to the castle, I’ll make that proposal.”
“But… is it really okay to just send you back to the castle like this?”

While I’m tilting my head in thought, Father continues talking with my Finacée. That’s right. What would happen if I were to send my Finacée directly back to the castle like this? Trash would be delighted, but given his history with Father, I can’t imagine a future where anything good comes of it.

“So you’ve turned yourself in, have you? Well then, the Shield Hero shall be put to death.” He might say something like that while fabricating a crime that never even happened. Or perhaps the Crimson Swine will set a trap or something to eliminate her before showing her to Trash. Either way, it’s safe to say the incident has happened a bit sooner than expected.
“Ideally, I’d like the Queen to handle this situation…”
“My mother is attending the World Conference while cleaning up after my father and older sister.”
“Do you know where it’s being held? For your own safety, I think it would be best if I escorted you there.”
“Well… the last time I saw her, she was in a country called Faubrey, but I don’t know which country she’s in now.”
That’s a difficult problem. Father let out a deep sigh.
“It’s hard to rely on the people of Melromarc, but if we turn to the people of Siltvelt, that would likely lead to war as well.”

The Shield Hero protecting Melromarc’s second princess… well, that’s not quite right. If it were seen as a capture, Siltvelt might seize the opportunity to start a war. Of course, there are certainly wise people there, and the Siltvelt envoy that Father spoke with was quite reasonable.

To begin with, Faubrey is dangerous in its own right. After all, Takt is there. Well, taking him out with a preemptive strike is one option, but if we kill him carelessly, remnants of his forces will likely emerge. Given the current situation, dealing with another problem would be a hassle. So, for now, it’s better to focus on the problem we’re currently facing.
“Father”
“What? Motoyasu-kun”
“Wouldn’t it be best to make it look like we’re hiding out in the country with my Finacée?”
“Well… I suppose so.”

That’s right—my future Father didn’t have a portal back then. It seemed he was hiding out in the country, waiting for an opportunity to leave. That’s when I caught him, and he fell into the Three Heroes Church’s trap. I don’t know why they took action sooner than the information I had suggested, but based on my knowledge of the future, the Three Heroes Church is about to become very active.
“So, Melty-chan, I’m sorry to ask this, but could you travel with us for a while? It’s dangerous—if things continue like this, you might end up as a victim of the Shield Hero.”
“I think I understand the situation. I’m sorry for the trouble. I’ll do my best.”
“Motoyasu and I will protect you as much as we can, so please don’t worry.”
“Yes. Judging by how strong you were just now, I understand that.”
Oh? My Finacée gave a slightly more down-to-earth reply.
“Anyway… Sakura-chan.”
“What?”
“I want you to prioritize protecting this girl over protecting me.”
“Got it!”
Sakura-chan stands in front of my Finacée to show she understands.
“Come on, hop on—Sakura will protect you!”
“Ah… okay.”

My fiancée climbed onto Sakura-chan’s back, looking a bit embarrassed. It seems her earlier tension has eased slightly. As expected, my rival, Filolial-sama, still finds peace of mind by being near her. Not to be outdone, I rub my cheek against Yuki-chan’s.
“Lord Motoyasu, that tickles.”
“Ho ho ho.”
“What’s Spear-Bro doing?”
“Boo?”
“Motoyasu-kun, don’t try to compete in a weird way. Be sure to keep a close eye on Elena-san, too. It looks like the Three Heroes Church is getting serious.”
“Boo…”
And over there, the Assistant is riding on my Rival’s back, greeting my Finacée.
“So there’s a dragon here, too. Are you all good friends?”
“Good friends… no.”
“I see. Filolials and dragons don’t get along, after all.”
“Aren’t you angry?”
“What good would getting angry do? That’s just how Filolials and dragons are, isn’t it?”
The Assistant nodded as if convinced by her Finacée’s words. Such composure! I feel like I’ve lost somehow. However, I’ll always be on Filolial-sama’s side, no matter what.
“Um, Shield Hero-sama.”
“What?”
“You really shouldn’t keep Filolials and dragons in the same place too much. Sakura-chan’s here…”

Of all things, my Finacée subtly pointed to the spot on Sakura-chan’s head where she’d gone bald from stress—a spot Sakura-chan hadn’t even noticed. At the same time, she pointed to the spot where my rival’s scales were missing.
“Ah… yeah. I’ll do my best to handle it as well as I can. Sorry about that.”
“Please do.”
“…My name is Wyndia. Can I call you Melty-chan?”

The assistant must have taken a liking to my finacée—who’d even noticed the condition of my rival’s scales—because she introduced herself on her own. And to think it took even Keel a while to trust him! Well, there’s really no benefit to getting along with an assistant who’s on good terms with a dragon, though.
“Sure.”
“Sakura—can I call you Mel-chan?”
“Sure.”
“It’s gotten lively again, hasn’t it…? For now, it looks like our priority is to keep an eye on the situation. We did manage to get rid of the witnesses, though.”

My father said this as he gazed off toward the distant castle of Melromarc. Come to think of it, because my Finacée had arrived, it had become difficult to go toward the castle. It wasn’t impossible, but we were now forced to wait and see how things played out. This was… the beginning of an incident—one that came a little too soon.
